A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IDO research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison; retained material can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments, ablations, noise-selection analyses and computational measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds weighting ablations, baseline comparisons and evaluations at additional noise levels.

M1.justification: The two-stage training procedure, class-specific beta mixture models, cleanliness/difficulty weights and three loss components remain unchanged. Equation 1 adds an explicit argmax, and Section 4.2 adjusts the squared-error terminology while retaining Equation 12; these edits do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: All six datasets and the image-classification task are retained. Appendix E.6 adds CIFAR-100 conditions with no noise, 80% symmetric noise, 20%/45% asymmetric noise and 20%/60% instance-dependent noise, extending corruption scenarios within existing coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 18 evaluates InstanceGM and NAL against IDO on CIFAR-100 under three noise settings. Figure 4 removes ELR from the efficiency comparison, although ELR remains in the accuracy tables. Other retained comparisons preserve their comparator membership.

E3.justification: New Table 6 introduces controlled comparisons using fixed difficulty weights of 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 against dynamic weighting. The existing main training budgets, architectures, data splits and optimizer configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 ablates loss components and examines baseline hyperparameter sensitivity. v4 additionally tests whether instance-dependent weighting itself is necessary through fixed-weight controls in Table 6, and tests robustness across clean and more severely corrupted data in Table 19. These substantially extend scrutiny of the central mechanism and its operating limits.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes from point estimates to mean-plus/minus reporting throughout the main synthetic-benchmark comparison. Both versions already report five random runs; additional runs are not established, and v4 does not define the ± statistic. Figure 2's caption also changes the reported central summary from median to mean while retaining the same graphic.

E6.justification: Tables 6, 18 and 19 add weighting, comparator and noise-level results. Table 19 newly shows IDO below UNICON at 80% symmetric noise, 62.5% versus 64.0%. Some retained values change beyond rounding: Table 1's Standard ResNet-50 accuracy at 20% symmetric CIFAR-100 noise changes from 75.5% to 75.19%. Figure 4 also removes ELR's accuracy/runtime entry.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 replaces the purported variance proof and its 1/T relative-change bound with a two-case derivation. v4 explicitly handles the undefined zero-to-one transition and bounds subsequent changes by 1/w_i^T, at most 1. This substantively revises the mathematical justification for wrong-event stability.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the claims of stable wrong-event modeling, instance-level dynamic optimization without additional tuning, superior accuracy and computational scalability. The new conclusion restates these contributions without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of why consistency learning benefits difficult samples, attributes InstanceGM's weaker results to conservative label correction, and interprets the new clean/high-noise results. Appendix E.6 associates degradation at 80% noise with mixture imbalance, but Section 6.1 retains v3's limitation referring to noise above 90%.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the anonymous code-release link with a named GitHub repository address. This changes the documented access information; repository availability was not independently checked. Appendix B's implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds the InstanceGM and Noise Attention Learning references and removes v3 references 15–18 concerning outlier summarization, Structure-Activation Synergy, GraphMaster and GraphOracle. The new weighting discussion explicitly connects IDO to Focal Loss, already cited in v3. The main related-work positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained. Local changes include rewriting Appendix C.2, adding experimental discussion and a conclusion, moving Appendix F's limitations to Section 6, and adding acknowledgments and the NeurIPS checklist. Author information and reference style are also reformatted.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a document-wide NeurIPS layout with narrower text, resized displays and a compact author block. It adds Tables 6, 18 and 19 and supplies Figure 8 for the previously described ROC analysis. Figure 4 is redrawn, corrects its accuracy-axis label and removes ELR; existing appendix tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new weighting controls and noise stress tests strengthen empirical scrutiny, while Appendix C.2 replaces v3's invalid 1/T argument with a more careful conditional bound. These provide a limited net improvement. Undefined ± statistics, the unreconciled 80% versus above-90% limitation, and removal of the faster ELR comparator from Figure 4 leave material reporting and claim-calibration weaknesses.
